events.outcome: Current Super guidance directly confirms the 180-day validity rule, EUR3 single-top-up threshold, 30-day receive-only recovery window, and eSIM starter availability.

Current Super first-party guidance still sells starter kits from €1 and confirms that calling-card service validity runs 180 days from activation or the last single top-up of at least €3. Splitting €3 into smaller top-ups does not extend validity. After expiry there is a 30-day receive/read/top-up rescue window; without a qualifying top-up the number and unused prepaid funds are lost.

Super continues to support both physical SIM and eSIM starter kits. Both standard SIM and eSIM can only be activated in Estonia; after activation the line can travel abroad with roaming enabled. Existing physical Super SIM cannot currently be converted directly to eSIM.

Roaming must be enabled before travel. In the EU, Super uses the same basic service price list as Estonia subject to fair-use rules. Outside the EU, operator prices vary and Super directs users to Telia roaming prices; this pass does not generalize non-EU inbound-SMS price or reachability into a reliability claim.

Super announced the basic standard-rate call and SMS price changing to €0.05 effective 24 September 2025. This does not replace the number-retention rule, which remains a single top-up of at least €3 every 180 days.

guideSteps: Buy a physical Super starter or eSIM starter while in Estonia.
Activate the physical SIM/eSIM in Estonia; overseas-first activation is not supported.
Before each 180-day validity deadline, make one single top-up of at least €3. Do not split it into smaller transactions.
If the 180-day period expires, use the 30-day receive/read/top-up rescue window before the number and prepaid balance are lost.
Enable roaming before travel; treat non-EU pricing and reachability as destination/network dependent rather than universally guaranteed.
